title: Riemann hypothesis
statement:
The **Riemann Hypothesis**: all non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function have real
part $\frac{1}{2}$. That is, if $\zeta(s) = 0$, $s \neq 1$, and $s$ is not a trivial zero
$-2(n+1)$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$, then $\operatorname{Re}(s) = \frac{1}{2}$.

This is the official Millennium Prize Problem as posed by the
[Clay Mathematics Institute](https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/riemann.pdf).

This uses the `RiemannHypothesis` type from Mathlib, which is defined as
`∀ (s : ℂ), riemannZeta s = 0 → (¬∃ n : ℕ, s = -2 * (n + 1)) → s ≠ 1 → s.re = 1 / 2`.
formal_statement: riemannHypothesis : RiemannHypothesis
scope_review: All zeros of the meromorphically continued zeta function, excluding s=1 and negative-even trivial zeros; real part exactly 1/2. The Dirichlet-series convergence half-plane is not the domain of the conjecture.
findings: The current Clay tracker labels RH unsolved. This supports a source-reported status, not a checked proof or exhaustive exclusion of recent claims. The pinned Lean signature aliases Mathlib's definition; its import closure and axioms were not executed.

title: Artin primitive roots: the selected density statement
statement:
**Artin's Conjecture on Primitive Roots**, second half.
Write $a = a_0 b^2$ where $a_0$ is squarefree. Under the conditions that $a$ is not a perfect
power and $a_0\not\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ (sequence A85397 in the OEIS), the density of the set
$S(a)$ of primes $p$ such that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ is independent of $a$ and
equals Artin's constant.
formal_statement:
artin_primitive_roots.parts.ii
    (a a_0 b : ℤ) (ha : a = a_0 * b ^ 2)
    (ha' : ∀ n m, m ≠ 1 → a ≠ n ^ m) (ha_0 : Squarefree a_0)
    (ha_0' : ¬a_0 ≡ 1 [ZMOD 4]) :
    (S a).HasDensity ArtinConstant {p | p.Prime}
scope_review: The selected density statement imposes a=a0*b^2, squarefree a0, no perfect-power representation and a0 not congruent to 1 modulo 4. This is not the unqualified all-integer constant-density claim.
findings: Pinned context explicitly says Hooley's conditional result needs RH for Dedekind zeta functions of Kummer fields, not merely Dirichlet GRH. No GRH-to-Artin edge is inferred from the imported RH problem. Degenerate a=0,+/-1 and perfect-power conventions need audit.

title: Beck–Fiala theorem and conjecture
statement:
**The Beck–Fiala conjecture**

There exists a universal constant $C > 0$ such that every set system
$S_1, \dots, S_m \subseteq [n]$ of degree at most $t$ admits a colouring
$\chi \colon [n] \to \{-1, +1\}$ with
$\left|\sum_{j \in S_i} \chi(j)\right| \le C \sqrt{t}$ for every $i$.
formal_statement:
beck_fiala_conjecture :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (n m t : ℕ) (S : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),
      (∀ j, (Finset.univ.filter fun i => j ∈ S i).card ≤ t) →
      ∃ χ : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ j, χ j = 1 ∨ χ j = -1) ∧
        ∀ i, |∑ j ∈ S i, χ j| ≤ C * Real.sqrt t
scope_review: A single universal C>0 works for all finite set systems with each element in at most t sets, with +/-1 coloring discrepancy <=C*sqrt(t). C cannot depend on n,m,t.
findings: The square-root conjecture must be separated from the classical linear-in-t theorem, logarithmic factors and algorithmic variants. This bounded search did not establish a current sharp universal theorem.

title: Resolution of singularities
statement:
**Resolution of singularities in positive characteristic.**
Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p > 0$ and let $X$ be an integral scheme that is
separated and of finite type over $k$. Then there is an integral scheme $Y$ that is smooth over
$k$ together with a proper birational morphism $Y \to X$.

This is open from dimension four on; see [Hau2010]. Perfectness of $k$ is needed for the
conclusion as stated; see `exists_not_hasResolution_of_not_perfectField`.
formal_statement:
resolution_of_singularities (k : Type u) [Field k] [PerfectField k] (p : ℕ)
    [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegral X]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType sX] [QuasiCompact sX] [IsSeparated sX] :
    Scheme.HasResolution sX
scope_review: Perfect positive-characteristic field; integral separated finite-type scheme; a proper birational morphism from a smooth integral scheme. Not arbitrary imperfect fields or merely alterations.
findings: Historical dimension-three results and programs with an unresolved termination step were found. Characteristic-zero resolution is outside the selected positive-characteristic scope. Imperfect-field counterexamples do not refute the perfect-field statement.

title: Serre's multiplicity conjectures
statement:
**Positivity conjecture.** Let $R$ be a regular local ring and let $M$, $N$ be finitely
generated $R$-modules such that $M \otimes_R N$ has finite length. If
$\dim M + \dim N = \dim R$, then $\chi(M, N) > 0$.

module is $\bot$.
formal_statement:
intersectionMultiplicity_pos (h : IsFiniteLength R (M ⊗[R] N))
    (hdim : Module.supportDim R M + Module.supportDim R N = ringKrullDim R) :
    0 < intersectionMultiplicity R M N
scope_review: Regular local ring, finitely generated modules with finite-length tensor product, and support dimensions summing to the ring dimension; intersection multiplicity strictly positive.
findings: Positivity, vanishing and nonnegativity are different Serre conjectures. Equicharacteristic and mixed-characteristic results cannot be transferred without matching hypotheses. The bounded search did not establish the full selected case.

title: Tournament anti-Sidorenko trees conjecture
statement:
**Tournament Anti-Sidorenko (TAS) Trees Conjecture.**

For every finite undirected tree $T$, there exists an orientation $\vec{T}$ of its edges such that
for any finite tournament $G$, the homomorphism density satisfies:
$$ t_{\vec{T}}(G) \le 2^{-e(T)} $$
where $e(T)$ is the total number of edges in $T$.
formal_statement:
tournament_anti_sidorenko_trees_conjecture :
    ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (T : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel T.Adj],
      T.IsTree →
      ∃ (D : Digraph V),
        D.IsOrientation T ∧
        ∀ {W : Type*} [Fintype W] [DecidableEq W] [Nonempty W]
          (G : Digraph W) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
          G.IsTournament →
          Digraph.homDensity D G ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ T.edgeFinset.card
scope_review: For each finite undirected tree, exists one orientation whose homomorphism density in every finite nonempty tournament is at most 2^(-edge count). Not the undirected Sidorenko conjecture.
findings: 2025/2026 papers establish particular orientations, paths and spiders and describe progress toward the universal statement. Quantifier order exists-orientation then all-tournaments is essential. No general solution is inferred from the title Sidorenko.

title: The 1/3–2/3 conjecture
statement:
Does every finite partially ordered set that is not totally ordered
contain two elements $x$ and $y$ such that the probability that
$x$ appears before $y$ in a random linear extension is between $\frac 1 3$ and $\frac 2 3$?

The set of all total order extensions is represented as order preserving
bijections $P$ of $1, ..., n$.
formal_statement:
conjecture_1_3_to_2_3 : ∀ (P : Type) [Finite P] [PartialOrder P]
    (not_total : ¬ Std.Total (α := P) (· ≤ ·)) (total_ext : Set <| OrderHom P ℕ)
    (total_ext_def : ∀ σ, σ ∈ total_ext ↔ Set.range σ = Set.Icc 1 (Nat.card P)),
    ∃ x y : P, ({σ ∈ total_ext | σ x < σ y}.ncard / total_ext.ncard : ℚ)
      ∈ Set.Icc (1/3) (2/3)
scope_review: Finite non-total partial order; uniform distribution on actual linear extensions; existence of a pair with probability in [1/3,2/3]. Source OrderHom encoding and bijectivity need correspondence checking.
findings: A September 2026 preprint announces improvement of a general lower balance bound, not a solution at 1/3. A 2017 paper gives particular poset families. Neither clears all finite nonchains.

title: The Bing-Borsuk Conjecture
statement:
The Bing-Borsuk Conjecture: every $n$-dimensional homogeneous absolute neighborhood retract
is a topological $n$-manifold. A topological space $X$ is an $n$-dimensional manifold
when `T2Space X ∧ Nonempty (ChartedSpace (Fin n → ℝ) X)`. The hypothesis `[MetrizableSpace X]`
implies `T2Space X` so this does not appear in the conclusion.
formal_statement:
bing_borsuk_conjecture : ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [MetrizableSpace X] [HomogeneousSpace X] [IsAbsoluteNeighborhoodRetract X],
    HasLebesgueCoveringDimensionEq X n → Nonempty (ChartedSpace (Fin n → ℝ) X)
scope_review: Metrizable homogeneous ANR of covering dimension n is a topological n-manifold, with the exact ChartedSpace/manifold separation and dimension conventions.
findings: Historical survey distinguishes Bing-Borsuk from Busemann and from weaker generalized-manifold assertions. A 2008 survey cannot alone certify current 2026 status. Source imports and ANR definitions have not been typechecked here.

title: Union-closed sets conjecture
statement:
For every finite union-closed family of sets, other than the family containing only the empty set,
there exists an element that belongs to at least half of the sets in the family.
formal_statement:
union_closed
    [Nonempty n]
    (h_ne_singleton_empty : A ≠ {∅})
    (h_union_closed : IsUnionClosed A) :
    ∃ i : n, (1 / 2 : ℚ) * #A ≤ #{x ∈ A | i ∈ x}
scope_review: Finite union-closed family, excluding the singleton family containing only the empty set, on a nonempty ground type; one element occurs in at least half of members. Empty-family case is vacuous under nonempty ground type.
findings: October 2026 work reports an improved lower frequency strictly below 1/2. This is progress toward, not a proof of, Frankl's half bound. Source's old 0.38234 comment is not a current best-bound claim.

title: Vizing's conjecture (1968)
statement:
**Vizing's conjecture (1968).**

For all finite simple graphs $G$ and $H$, the domination number of the Cartesian (box)
product satisfies $\gamma(G \,\square\, H) \ge \gamma(G)\,\gamma(H)$.
formal_statement:
vizing_conjecture :
    ∀ {α β : Type} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
      (G : SimpleGraph α) (H : SimpleGraph β),
      G.dominationNumber * H.dominationNumber ≤ (G □ H).dominationNumber
scope_review: All finite simple graphs G,H: domination number of Cartesian product at least the product of domination numbers. Not Vizing's edge-coloring theorem or other graph products.
findings: An old claimed full proof and a later almost-all-pairs result were both found. A proof-title claim is not sufficient acceptance evidence. Exact hypotheses of each paper must be inspected before changing universal status.

title: Černý Conjecture
statement:
**Černý Conjecture**: Every synchronizing DFA with $n$ states admits a
synchronizing word of length at most $(n - 1)^2$.
formal_statement:
cerny_conjecture :
    ∀ {α : Type*} {σ : Type*} [Fintype σ] (M : DFA α σ) (hM : M.IsSynchronizing) ,
    ∃ w : List α, M.IsSynchronizingWord w ∧ w.length ≤ (Fintype.card σ - 1)^2
scope_review: Every synchronizing finite-state DFA with n states has a reset word of length at most (n-1)^2. Existence of a longer bound or examples attaining the lower bound do not prove the conjecture.
findings: State count, alphabet finiteness and synchronization definitions must match. Current sharp general upper bounds and recent proof claims were not established by this pass; source remains unverified.

title: Gauss circle problem
statement:
It is conjectured that the correct bound is
$$
  |E(r)| = O\left(r^{1/2 + o(1)}\right)
$$

[Ha59]  Hardy, G. H. (1959). _Ramanujan: Twelve Lectures on Subjects Suggested by His Life and Work_(3rd ed.). New York: Chelsea Publishing Company. p. 67

See also https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.03549
formal_statement:
error_isBigO : ∃ (o : ℝ → ℝ) (_ : Tendsto o atTop (𝓝 0)),
    E =O[atTop] fun r => r ^ (1/2 + o r)
scope_review: Error term for lattice points in a disk as radius tends to infinity; requested O(r^(1/2+o(1))). Radius and squared-radius conventions change exponents.
findings: No current best exponent is asserted. Big-O constants, radius normalization and equivalence between o(1)-exponent and all-epsilon formulations need an explicit analytic comparison.

title: Graceful Tree Conjecture (Ringel–Kotzig conjecture)
statement:
Every tree admits a graceful labeling.

A graceful labeling of a tree $T$ with $m$ edges is an injective map $f : V \to \{0, \dots, m\}$
such that the multiset of absolute differences $|f(u) - f(v)|$ over edges $\{u,v\}$ of $T$
equals $\{1, \dots, m\}$.
formal_statement:
graceful_tree_conjecture {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (T : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel T.Adj] (hT : T.IsTree) :
    let m := T.edgeFinset.card
    ∃ f : V → ℕ,
      Function.Injective f ∧
      (∀ v, f v ≤ m) ∧
      T.edgeFinset.image (fun e =>
        e.lift ⟨fun u v => Int.natAbs ((f u : ℤ) - (f v : ℤ)),
                fun u v => by
                  show ((f u : ℤ) - f v).natAbs = ((f v : ℤ) - f u).natAbs
                  rw [← Int.natAbs_neg, neg_sub]⟩) = Finset.Icc 1 m
scope_review: Every finite simple tree with m edges has an injective labeling in0..m whose absolute edge differences are exactly1..m. Not approximate label ranges or a bounded-order computation.
findings: A paper reports checking trees up to35 vertices and another proves an approximate asymptotic relaxation. Neither proves the exact all-tree statement. An old full-proof title is not accepted without checking its argument and status.
